ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • The term 'UFO' was officially created in 1953 by the United States Air Force as a catch-all for airborne objects that could not be identified as known aircraft or familiar objects.
  • Upon investigation, most reported UFOs are identified as known objects, natural phenomena, hoaxes, or mirages, while a small number remain unexplained.
  • Project Blue Book analyzed 12,618 UFO reports from 1952 to 1969; 701 cases remained classified as 'unidentified'.
  • The June 2021 ODNI preliminary assessment examined 144 UAP reports from U.S. government sources (2004-2021); all but one (a deflating balloon) remained unidentified.
  • NASA's UAP Independent Study Team (final report, September 14, 2023) found no evidence of extraterrestrial origin and recommended a rigorous, evidence-based approach with better data collection.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Kenneth Arnold (1947) — Reported nine shiny unidentified objects past Mount Rainier, estimating speeds of at least 1,200 mph; his account coined the 'flying saucer' era.
  • David Fravor (2004) — Retired U.S. Navy Commander; reported a white, oval, ~40-foot object hovering over a disturbed ocean patch off San Diego that mirrored his F/A-18's maneuvers and vanished at extraordinary speed.
  • Alex Dietrich (2004) — Retired U.S. Navy Lt. Commander; Fravor's wingman and corroborating witness to the 2004 Nimitz Tic Tac encounter.

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • Project Blue Book — U.S. Air Force, 1952-1969: No reported UFO was ever an indication of a threat to national security; no evidence the 'unidentified' cases were extraterrestrial vehicles or technology beyond modern science.
  • Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena — Office of the Director of National Intelligence / UAP Task Force, 2021: 143 of 144 reports remained unexplained due to limited data; 18 incidents showed unusual flight characteristics; no evidence linked sightings to extraterrestrial life.
  • UAP Independent Study Team — NASA, 2022-2023: No evidence of extraterrestrial origin found; recommended NASA play a prominent role using its Earth-observing assets and rigorous data collection.

  • The military said it had been conducting no test flights during the time of Arnold's sighting, though Arnold himself first suspected experimental military aircraft.

  • The debris came from a complex uncrewed military balloon train operated from Alamogordo Army Air Field as part of the top-secret Project Mogul - a program to detect Soviet nuclear tests via sound waves in the upper atmosphere; specifically NYU Flight 4, launched June 4, 1947.
  • In the 1990s the U.S. Air Force published official reports (1994 and 1997) concluding the recovered material was consistent with a Project Mogul balloon, not a UFO.
  • The 1997 report ('Case Closed') concluded the 'alien body' accounts likely reflected witnesses misremembering anthropomorphic dummies used in 1950s high-altitude parachute tests.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • William 'Mac' Brazel (1947) — Rancher who found the metallic and rubber debris on his land and reported it, triggering the Army's involvement.
  • Jesse Marcel (1978) — Retired USAF Major; in 1978 claimed the Army's weather-balloon story was a cover and speculated the debris was extraterrestrial - the claim that revived the Roswell legend via the 1980 book 'The Roswell Incident'.

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • The Roswell Report — U.S. Air Force, 1994 and 1997: Debris was consistent with a Project Mogul balloon train; the 'bodies' accounts traced to misremembered 1950s anthropomorphic dummy tests. No evidence of extraterrestrial craft.

  • The American Academy of Sleep Medicine's 2018 position paper recommends imagery rehearsal therapy (IRT) — recalling the nightmare, rewriting it with positive changes, and rehearsing the new version — as the first-line behavioral treatment for repetitive nightmares.

  • In February 2021, four independent labs published in Current Biology the first demonstrated two-way communication with lucid dreamers: experimenters asked questions via spoken messages, tones, lights, or touch, and dreaming participants answered with specific eye movements.
  • LaBerge's MILD (mnemonic induction of lucid dreams) technique — rehearsing the intention to recognize dreaming while awake — remains a standard induction method.

  • The rectory was badly damaged by fire in 1939 and demolished in 1944.
  • After Price's death in 1948, the Society for Psychical Research published its 'Borley Report' (The Haunting of Borley Rectory, 1956), concluding many phenomena were faked or had natural causes; Price's claims are now generally discredited by ghost historians.

  • Marianne Foyster (1930-1935) — Wife of rector Lionel Foyster; reported phenomena at the rectory during 1930-1935, but later research (SPR report; Terence Hines) found she was actively fabricating haunted phenomena.

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • The term 'Bermuda Triangle' was coined in 1964 by writer Vincent Gaddis in an Argosy magazine article, and retroactively applied to a roughly 500,000-to-1.5-million-square-mile region of the North Atlantic.
  • Flight 19: on December 5, 1945, five U.S. Navy TBM Avenger bombers (14 crew) vanished on a training flight from Fort Lauderdale after leader Lt. Charles Taylor became disoriented; a PBM Mariner rescue plane (13 crew) also disappeared that day.
  • USS Cyclops: in March 1918, the Navy cargo ship vanished between Barbados and the Chesapeake Bay with 306 crew and 10,000 tons of manganese ore, without sending an SOS.
  • Arizona State librarian Larry Kusche's 1975 book The Bermuda Triangle Mystery-Solved showed the 'mystery' was manufactured: incidents were misreported, exaggerated, or had mundane causes (storms, navigational error, mechanical failure), and the area's loss rate is no higher than other heavily traveled regions.

  • Larry Kusche archival research — independent researcher (Arizona State University librarian), 1975: Published The Bermuda Triangle Mystery-Solved: most incidents had ordinary explanations; many were misreported or never occurred in the area; the 'Triangle' is a manufactured mystery.

  • The FBI wrote: 'Once the body starts to burn, there is enough fat and other inflammable substances to permit varying amounts of destruction to take place... almost complete combustion of the body.'
  • Skeptical investigator Joe Nickell's analysis concluded there is no verified case of genuine spontaneous combustion; the 'wick effect' has been demonstrated experimentally.

  • Joe Nickell SHC analysis — Skeptical Inquirer (Center for Inquiry), Investigative Files, 1996: No authenticated case of spontaneous human combustion exists; alleged cases consistently involve an external ignition source (cigarette, pipe) plus the wick effect.

  • Folklore in many cultures (the Norse vardoger, the Celtic fetch) treats seeing one's own double as an omen of death; modern neurology links such experiences to autoscopic hallucinations and disorders of self-perception, not to physical doubles.

  • Project MKUltra was a CIA program of research into behavioral modification, authorized by CIA Director Allen Dulles in April 1953 and run by chemist Sidney Gottlieb of the CIA's Technical Services Division, ending in 1973.
  • The program comprised about 149 subprojects involving psychoactive drugs (notably LSD and mescaline), hypnosis, sensory deprivation, isolation and other chemical, biological and psychological methods, including experiments on unwitting subjects.
  • CIA safehouses run by narcotics agent George White (e.g., Operation Midnight Climax in San Francisco, from 1956) were used for covert administration of drugs to unwitting subjects.
  • In January 1973, CIA Director Richard Helms ordered the destruction of the MKUltra files; in 1977 a FOIA search turned up seven misfiled boxes of financial records covering ~149 subprojects, which form the bulk of the surviving record.
  • Biochemist Frank Olson died in 1953 after being unwittingly dosed with LSD at Deep Creek Lodge; a 1963 Inspector General report surviving the file destruction documented the program's abuses.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Frank Olson (1953 (death); investigations 1975) — U.S. Army biochemist who died in 1953 after being unwittingly administered LSD by CIA personnel at Deep Creek Lodge; fell from his Hotel Statler window. The Church Committee and Rockefeller Commission confirmed his death was linked to the program.
  • John Marks (1977-1979) — Investigative journalist who obtained ~16,000 surviving MKUltra documents via FOIA in 1977 and reconstructed the program in his book 'The Search for the Manchurian Candidate' (1979); his archive anchors the public record of the surviving files.

  • Project MKUltra Senate hearing — U.S. Senate (Select Committee on Intelligence / Human Resources), 1977: Joint Senate hearing (Kennedy committee) with CIA Director Stansfield Turner; documented ~149 subprojects from recovered fiscal records and put the program fully on the public record.

  • Despite decades of direct-detection experiments (LZ, XENONnT deep underground; the Large Hadron Collider), no dark matter particle has been conclusively detected.
  • Leading candidate particles include WIMPs (weakly interacting massive particles) and axions; upcoming mapping by the Vera C. Rubin Observatory and ESA's Euclid mission will trace dark matter via gravitational lensing.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • KIC 8462852 (Tabby's Star / Boyajian's Star) is an F-type main-sequence star in the constellation Cygnus, ~1,470 light-years from Earth.
  • Its bizarre light curve — irregular, aperiodic dips of up to ~22% (a 15% dip around day 800 and a deeper ~22% sequence ~two years later) — was found in 2015 by Tabetha Boyajian's team with Planet Hunters citizen scientists in NASA Kepler data; a normal transiting planet causes <1% dips.
  • The 'alien megastructure' (Dyson sphere/swarm) idea was proposed only as a hypothesis of last resort; a 2018 multiwavelength campaign led by Boyajian showed the dimming is wavelength-dependent (more blue light blocked), consistent with fine dust — not an opaque megastructure.
  • Breakthrough Listen observed the star with the Green Bank Telescope and found no artificial radio signals.
  • A July 2026 study (Madurga-Favieres et al., MNRAS) proposed a giant planet shepherding exocomets as the dust source; the exact cause remains unsettled.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Tabetha Boyajian (2015) — Astrophysicist who led the team that characterized KIC 8462852's bizarre dimming in 2015; the star is nicknamed 'Tabby's Star' after her.
  • Jason Wright (2018) — Penn State astronomer who co-led the follow-up analysis concluding the dips are 'for sure not aliens' — consistent with boring old dust.
  • Planet Hunters citizen scientists (2015) — Volunteer citizen scientists who flagged the star's anomalous light curve in Kepler data, enabling the discovery.

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • Breakthrough Listen observations of Tabby's Star — Breakthrough Listen (Green Bank Telescope), 2015-2016: No artificial radio emission detected; null result for technosignatures.
  • Multiwavelength dimming campaign — Boyajian et al. (Astrophysical Journal Letters, 2018), 2018: Wavelength-dependent dimming consistent with dust clouds (exocomets/debris), not an opaque alien megastructure.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • The first fast radio burst (FRB 010724, the 'Lorimer Burst') was identified in 2007 by Duncan Lorimer and his student David Narkevic in archival 2001 data from the Parkes radio telescope in Australia; the 4.6-millisecond pulse came from billions of light-years away.
  • FRBs are millisecond-duration radio flashes from other galaxies; the Lorimer burst released in one millisecond roughly as much energy as the Sun emits in ~80 years.
  • FRB 121102, discovered in 2015 by Paul Scholz in Arecibo archival data, was the first repeating FRB; it was localized to a dwarf galaxy ~2.5-3 billion light-years away.
  • The CHIME telescope detected a second repeater (FRB 180814) in 2018-2019; ~100+ FRB sources were catalogued within a decade of the first discovery.
  • In 2019 the Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder traced a one-off FRB to a massive, tranquil host galaxy — different from the active dwarf host of the repeater, suggesting multiple source types.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Duncan Lorimer and David Narkevic (2007) — Found the first FRB (FRB 010724, the 'Lorimer Burst') in 2007 while re-analyzing archival Parkes pulsar-survey data from 2001.
  • Paul Scholz (2015) — Discovered the first repeating fast radio burst (FRB 121102) in 2015 in archival Arecibo Observatory data.

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • CHIME FRB Project — Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME), Canada, 2018-present: Detected 13 FRBs in mid-2018 including the second-ever repeating burst (FRB 180814); now the leading FRB discovery engine.
  • ASKAP FRB localization — CSIRO / Australian Square Kilometre Array Pathfinder, 2019: Pinpointed a one-off FRB to its host galaxy, showing one-off and repeating FRBs may be different phenomena.

SOURCES & REFERENCES:
  • A brief history: What we know so far about fast radio bursts across the universe - Phys.org — https://phys.org/news/2021-02-history-fast-radio-universe.html
  • Why hunting for fast radio bursts is an 'exploding field' in astronomy - Phys.org — https://phys.org/news/2019-07-fast-radio-field-astronomy.html
  • A lone fast radio burst was traced to its home for the first time - Science News — https://www.sciencenews.org/article/telescopes-tracked-fast-radio-burst-faraway-galaxy

CAVEAT: The astrophysical origin of FRBs is still unknown; all currently favored explanations are natural — no confirmed artificial source.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • Rogue (free-floating) planets are worlds not gravitationally bound to any star — either ejected from a planetary system or formed in isolation like a failed star.
  • PSO J318.5-22, discovered in 2013 by Michael Liu's team (University of Hawaii) in Pan-STARRS PS1 data, is ~80 light-years away with ~8.3 Jupiter masses, ~1,100 K surface temperature, and an age of ~23 million years (Beta Pictoris moving group).
  • WISE 0855−0714, discovered in 2014 by Kevin Luhman, is the coldest known brown dwarf/rogue planet (~250 K, colder than Earth's North Pole) at just ~7.2 light-years away.
  • Microlensing surveys are the only way to find them: OGLE-2016-BLG-1928 (2020) was the first credible Earth-mass rogue planet candidate.
  • A 2023 analysis of a nine-year MOA microlensing survey (Takahiro Sumi, Osaka University; NASA Goddard) estimated ~20 free-floating planets per star in the Milky Way — potentially trillions — though with very broad uncertainty.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Michael Liu (2013) — Led the University of Hawaii team that discovered PSO J318.5-22 (2013) in Pan-STARRS data — the first well-studied free-floating planetary-mass object.
  • Kevin Luhman (2014) — Discovered WISE 0855−0714 (2014), the coldest known rogue planetary-mass object (~250 K), 7.2 light-years away.
  • Przemek Mróz (2020) — Led the OGLE team reporting OGLE-2016-BLG-1928 (2020), the first credible Earth-mass rogue planet detection via microlensing.

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • MOA nine-year microlensing survey — Microlensing Observations in Astrophysics (Osaka University + NASA Goddard), 2023 (published): Free-floating planets may outnumber stars ~20-to-1 (trillions galaxy-wide); estimate is statistical, with large uncertainty.
  • Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope rogue-planet survey — NASA, Planned launch by May 2027: Planned census: expected to find up to ~400 Earth-mass rogue worlds and measure the free-floating-planet population directly.

SOURCES & REFERENCES:
  • PSO J318.5−22 - Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PSO_J318.5−22
  • NASA researchers estimate Milky Way holds 20x more rogue planets than stars - Space Daily — https://spacedaily.com/t-milky-way-20-times-more-rogue-planets-than-stars/
  • How Gravitational Microlensing Works - IEEE Spectrum — https://spectrum.ieee.org/rogue-planet/how-gravitational-microlensing-works

CAVEAT: Population counts of rogue planets are statistical extrapolations from a handful of microlensing events with broad uncertainty — not a direct census.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • THEORETICAL — In 1957 Hugh Everett III, in his Princeton PhD thesis supervised by John Wheeler, proposed the 'relative state formulation': the universal wave function never collapses; every quantum measurement outcome is physically realized in a separate, non-interacting branch of reality.
  • The term 'many-worlds' was coined and popularized by physicist Bryce DeWitt in the 1960s-1970s (Physics Today 1970; edited volume 1973).
  • Many-worlds is now considered a mainstream interpretation of quantum mechanics alongside Copenhagen and others, with modern advocates including David Deutsch, Sean Carroll, and Max Tegmark.
  • It makes the same empirical predictions as standard quantum mechanics with wave-function collapse, so no experiment can currently distinguish it — the disagreement is interpretive, not empirical.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Hugh Everett III (1957) — American physicist who proposed the relative-state formulation (many-worlds) in his 1957 Princeton doctoral thesis.
  • Bryce DeWitt (1970s) — Physicist who popularized Everett's formulation in the 1960s-70s and coined the term 'many-worlds'.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • A small ceramic jar (~13–15 cm tall) containing a copper cylinder and an iron rod sealed with bitumen, found at Khujut Rabu near Baghdad; the assemblage surfaced in 1936 excavations of a Parthian/Sasanian-period site (c. 150 BCE–650 CE).
  • German archaeologist Wilhelm König described the jars in 1938 and published the galvanic-cell hypothesis in 1940, suggesting they were used to electroplate gold onto silver.
  • Modern replicas filled with vinegar, lemon juice, or grape juice produce about 0.5–1.1 volts per jar.
  • On the 29th episode (23 March 2005) of Discovery Channel's MythBusters, ten hand-made jar replicas connected in series produced 4.33 volts — enough to electroplate a small copper token with zinc overnight; verdict: 'plausible.'
  • Mainstream archaeologists remain skeptical: no wiring, no electroplated artifacts, and no supporting infrastructure have been found; similar vessels at Seleucia and Ctesiphon appear to have held sacred scrolls. In 2012, Stony Brook archaeologist Elizabeth Stone said she knew 'not a single archaeologist' who believed they were batteries.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Wilhelm König (1938–1940) — German archaeologist who described the Khujut Rabu jar assemblage in 1938 and published the hypothesis that they were ancient galvanic cells (1940).
  • Willard Gray (1940s) — American engineer who, after WWII, built a reconstruction that produced electric current when filled with grape juice.
  • Arne Eggebrecht (1978) — Egyptologist who in 1978 used a recreation filled with grape juice to reportedly electroplate a silver statuette in two hours; no photographic records survive, and skeptics doubt the experiment's validity.
  • Elizabeth Stone (2012) — Stony Brook University Iraqi-archaeology expert who stated in 2012 that she does not know a single archaeologist who believed the jars were batteries.

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • Baghdad Battery test — Discovery Channel (MythBusters), episode 29, 2005: Ten replica jars in series produced 4.33 volts and could electroplate a small copper token with zinc overnight and deliver painful current through acupuncture needles — but archaeologist Ken Feder noted there is no evidence jars were ever wired together or used for plating. Verdict: plausible, but doubtful as actual ancient practice.

  • In the late 20th century, metallurgist J. D. Verhoeven (Iowa State) and bladesmith Alfred Pendray chemically analyzed historic blades and reproduced wootz with microscopically and visually identical patterns, identifying trace vanadium (~0.005%) plus repeated thermal cycling as the key.
  • A 2006 Nature study by Reibold et al. (TU Dresden) found carbon nanotubes enclosing cementite nanowires in a 17th-century Damascus sabre — an unintended byproduct of the forging process, not consciously engineered nanotech.
  • Modern makers (e.g., Dierk Raabe's team at the Max Planck Institute) now 3D-print modern facsimiles of Damascus steel, replicating the layered hardening with far less energy.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • Turritopsis dohrnii is a ~4.5 mm hydrozoan jellyfish, found worldwide in temperate to tropical waters, that can revert from a sexually mature medusa back to the immature polyp stage when stressed, injured, starving, or aging - the only known animal that can do this after reaching adulthood.
  • The reversal works by transdifferentiation: specialized medusa cells (muscle, nerve, stinging cells) revert to an unspecialized state and redifferentiate as polyp cells; the cycle can in theory repeat indefinitely, making the animal biologically immortal.
  • The reversal was first noticed in the 1990s by German graduate student Christian Sommer in Rapallo, Italy, and formally published in 1996 by Piraino, Boero and colleagues in the Biological Bulletin.
  • A 2022 PNAS whole-genome study (Pascual-Torner, Lopez-Otin and colleagues, University of Oviedo) found T. dohrnii carries roughly double the genes for DNA repair and damage protection of its sister species T. rubra; this finding was formally contested in PNAS in 2023 by Maria Pia Miglietta (Texas A&M), so the genetic basis is still unsettled.
  • In nature most individuals never get to reverse: they die from predation or disease as medusae; in labs, specimens have been documented running the cycle more than ten times in succession.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Christian Sommer (1990s) — German graduate student who, while studying hydrozoans at Rapallo, Italy, noticed adult Turritopsis medusae in his petri dishes were not dying when stressed but reverting to the polyp stage
  • Shin Kubota (1990s-present) — Marine biologist at Kyoto University's Seto Marine Biological Laboratory who has kept and repeatedly cycled Turritopsis dohrnii through life-cycle reversals in the laboratory for years

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • Comparative genomics of mortal and immortal cnidarians (whole-genome assembly) — University of Oviedo (Pascual-Torner, Lopez-Otin et al.), published in PNAS, 2022: Found approximately doubled DNA-repair/damage-protection gene copies and variants affecting cell-division and telomere stability in T. dohrnii vs T. rubra; formally challenged in PNAS 2023 (Miglietta), so the genetic basis remains contested.
  • Reverse-development experiment on Turritopsis life cycle — Piraino, Boero, Aeschbach and Schmid; published in Biological Bulletin, 1996: First formal documentation that adult Turritopsis medusae can revert to the polyp stage, establishing the mechanism of life-cycle reversal.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • Tardigrades (phylum Tardigrada) are 0.1-1.5 mm invertebrates with eight legs that enter a desiccated dormant 'tun' state (cryptobiosis/anhydrobiosis), surviving extreme drying, heat, cold, pressure, and radiation.
  • In September 2007 the European Space Agency flew about 3,000 desiccated tardigrades on the FOTON-M3 mission (BIOPAN-6) into low Earth orbit, exposing them for 10 days to open space vacuum and solar UV; Jönsson et al. reported in Current Biology (2008) that 68 percent of Milnesium tardigradum revived within 30 minutes of rehydration in the UV-A/UV-B group, while vacuum alone caused almost no mortality - the first animal ever confirmed to survive direct exposure to open space.
  • The same 2007 TARDIS experiment showed full-spectrum solar UV was far deadlier: only three Milnesium tardigradum individuals survived that group, though survivors later reproduced normally.
  • In May 2011, tardigrades flew aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Endeavour (STS-134) to the International Space Station for the TARDIKISS experiment (Angela Maria Rizzo et al.): 98.33 percent of Paramacrobiotus richtersi and 90 percent of Ramazzottius oberhaeuseri survived, and microgravity plus cosmic radiation 'did not significantly affect survival of tardigrades in flight'.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • None documented. (N/A) — N/A

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • TARDIS / TARSE / RoTaRad (BIOPAN-6) — European Space Agency, FOTON-M3 mission (reported by Jönsson et al. in Current Biology), 2007-2008: Tardigrades survived open-space vacuum and cosmic radiation; ~68% of Milnesium tardigradum revived within 30 minutes after UV-A/UV-B exposure, but only 3 individuals survived full solar UV spectrum.
  • TARDIKISS (Tardigrades in Space) — Angela Maria Rizzo et al., University of Modena; flew on STS-134 Endeavour / ISS, 2011: Microgravity and cosmic radiation 'did not significantly affect survival of tardigrades in flight'; 98.33% survival for P. richtersi and 90% for R. oberhaeuseri.

  • Clairvius Narcisse of Haiti was pronounced dead in 1962 (his death certificate was signed by two American doctors at the Albert Schweitzer Hospital, and his sister identified the body) - then walked back into his village in 1980, eighteen years later, claiming he had spent years as a zombie on a sugar plantation after being exhumed and enslaved by a bokor.
  • Canadian ethnobotanist Wade Davis investigated Haitian zombification in 1982-1983 and argued in his controversial 1985 book The Serpent and the Rainbow that zombie powder containing tetrodotoxin (pufferfish toxin) and bufotoxin (toad toxin) induced a deathlike coma, followed by dosing with the deliriant Datura stramonium to keep victims compliant; critics found his methodology unscientific and could not confirm the toxin claims from his samples.
  • Haitian psychiatrist Lamarque Douyon spent decades studying zombie accounts and, convinced drugging was involved, connected American colleagues with the cases that led Davis to Haiti.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • Clairvius Narcisse (1962-1980) — Haitian man whose death was certified in 1962; reappeared in 1980 claiming he had been exhumed and kept as a zombie by a bokor who had 'taken his soul'
  • Wade Davis (1982-1983) — Harvard ethnobotanist who investigated zombie cases in Haiti and reported that zombie powders contained tetrodotoxin and bufotoxin capable of mimicking death
  • Lamarque Douyon (1970s-1980s) — Haitian psychiatrist who studied zombie accounts for decades and brought them to the attention of US researchers

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • Ethnobotanical investigation of Haitian zombification — Wade Davis, Harvard University (published as The Serpent and the Rainbow), 1982-1985: Hypothesized that tetrodotoxin-based zombie powder plus Datura stramonium produced apparent death and a compliant 'zombie' state; the findings were widely publicized but scientifically contested by other researchers.

  • FOLKLORE: Arnold Paole of Medveđa, Serbia, a hajduk who claimed to have been plagued by a vampire in Gossowa and cured himself with grave soil and the vampire's blood, died about 1725 after falling from a haywagon; 40 days later villagers exhumed him, found the corpse 'undecomposed' with fresh blood at the eyes, nose, mouth and ears, drove a stake through his heart, beheaded and burned the body, and did the same to his four supposed victims.
  • FOLKLORE: The panic recurred in Medveđa in the winter of 1731-1732, when more than ten people died within weeks; this second outbreak drew an official Austrian military medical commission.

  • The animals were almost certainly West Indian manatees (Trichechus manatus): the location, habitat, behavior, and number match manatee behavior, and Columbus had previously seen similar animals off the Grain Coast of Guinea.
  • The scientific order for manatees and dugongs is Sirenia, named for the sirens of Greek myth - whose features (ability to turn the head, fingerlike bones in the forelimbs, 'tail stands' in shallow water) make them look humanlike from a distance.
  • FOLKLORE: The mermaid idea predates Columbus by millennia: Homer's Odyssey features deadly sirens, and the 4th-century BC Babylonian god Oannes was a half-fish, half-human being who left the sea each day.

ESTABLISHED FACTS & MEASUREMENTS:
  • Since the early 1990s, some residents of Taos, New Mexico, have reported a persistent low-frequency hum or drone, often compared to a distant idling diesel engine, louder indoors and at night, with some hearers reporting headaches, sleep disturbance, and fatigue; most people hear nothing.
  • A survey of 8,000 residents found that 161 (about 2 percent) could hear it; hearers each reported a different perceived frequency between about 32 and 80 Hz, modulated 0.5 to 2 Hz.
  • No microphone or recording device has ever captured a sound matching what hearers describe; the phenomenon has also been reported in other regions (the 'Hum' is not unique to Taos).
  • Main candidate explanations - tinnitus, industrial/infrasound sources, elevated electromagnetic fields near power lines - have never been confirmed; the cause remains officially unresolved.

NAMED WITNESS REPORTS:
  • None documented. (N/A) — N/A

PUBLIC INVESTIGATIONS:
  • 1993 Taos Hum scientific study (final report 1995) — University of New Mexico (led by Joe Mullins) with Los Alamos National Laboratory, Sandia National Laboratories, and Phillips Air Force Laboratory; commissioned at the request of U.S. Rep. Bill Richardson, 1993-1995: Inconclusive: no acoustic, seismic, or electromagnetic source matching the hearers' descriptions was identified; hearers each perceived a different frequency, and only an elevated electromagnetic field near power lines was noted.
